method.value: Start from MAST rate.fits; correct 1/f noise, mask snowballs, apply custom sky flats, subtract wisps and apply photometric corrections.

evidence.quote: We start with the MAST `rate.fits` products produced by Stage 1 of the *JWST* calibration pipeline (v1.8.4) using calibration set `jwst_0995.pmap`.
We derive a correction for the “$1/f$ noise” (cite: rauscher:15) by subtracting the source-masked median image values computed along detector rows and columns.
After applying the flat-field calibration, we fit and subtract the additive “wisp” structure in some of the short-wavelength filter/detector combinations (cite: Rigby:22) using wisp templates

why_this_data.value: Gravitational lensing pushes the imaging and spectroscopy beyond blank-field depths; Abell 2744 also has complementary data and ALMA access.

evidence.quote: The imaging and spectroscopy leverages the gravitational lensing boost to push beyond depths achievable in blank fields.

The field also contains some of the best complementary multi-wavelength data (including deep $29$AB *HST*/ACS optical data) and is accessible by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA)

why_this_method.value: Four-pointing gap-filled NIRCam mosaic maximizes predicted z>10 galaxy detections.

evidence.quote: The number of $z{>}10$ galaxies is maximized by a 4-pointing gap-filled NIRCam mosaic.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Mask snowball residuals rather than rerun exposure ramp fits.

evidence.quote: Rather than re-running the ramp fits, we identify likely snowballs as large groups of pixels with the $\mathrm{DQ}=4$ bit set in the exposure data quality array and grow a conservative mask around them.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Use uniform custom sky flats despite updated in-flight long-wavelength CRDS flats.

evidence.quote: however, we use the custom sky flats that were computed in a uniform way for all short- and long-wavelength filter/detector combinations.

limitations_admitted.value: Weight maps omit correlated noise from drizzle resampling.

evidence.quote: The weight map does not account for correlated noise of the finite drizzle pixel resampling (cite: casertano:00).

limitations_admitted.value: Masked pixels reduce local effective exposure time.

evidence.quote: Any masked pixels will not contribute to the mosaic and the total effective exposure time at those positions will therefore decrease.

limitations_admitted.value: Wavelength-dependent MSA slit losses complicate precise spectroscopic flux calibration.

evidence.quote: Slit loss through the MSA will be significant and wavelength dependent due to variation in the PSF, complicating precise flux calibration.

limitations_admitted.value: Theoretical models dominate uncertainty in predicted galaxy counts.

evidence.quote: The dominant uncertainty in expected numbers is the difference between theoretical models, which can differ by factors of $>10$ at $z>10$

limitations_admitted.value: Some NIRSpec observations failed and required repeat visits.

evidence.quote: The spectroscopic component of the UNCOVER survey were completed in July-August 2023, aside from a failed visit that was impacted by an electrical short.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA is ancillary context; this paper supplies no original ALMA measurements or ALMA analysis recipe.
The calibration and imaging setting lists are restricted to ALMA; the numbered recipe describes the explicitly documented JWST mosaic work.
Table 2 lists ALMA times under Notes/Depth without establishing that they are on-source integration times.
Depths describe point sources in two-visit regions, not uniform completeness across the mosaics or extended-source sensitivity.
Weight-map depths require scrutiny because the stated weight maps omit drizzle-correlated noise.
Predicted galaxy counts and future spectroscopic capabilities are not measured galaxy-population results.
